title: EMW-1.0 Inventory And Implementation-Fit Record
summary: historical inventory plus completed counts-only external-media relocation used by EMW-1.1
content_html:
EMW-1.0 Inventory And Implementation-Fit Record

Checkpoint Result

EMW-1 fits the existing provider adapters, media services, renderer, transfer planner, scope lifecycle, and explicit Publish gate without a general asset registry, content-addressed store, dual reader, or provider-search fallback. The implementation is broad because the current published.media contract combines private authority, served URL, build output, and public exposure; EMW-1 must split those responsibilities in one schema and authority cutover.

This record began as the temporary EMW-1.0 review authority. The user subsequently approved a direct relocation, created the target folders, and moved or copied the files. The proposed manifest-and-hash migration ceremony below is retained only as historical planning context and is not a delivery requirement. EMW-1 now owns the completed EMW-1.1 and EMW-1.2 evidence and is parked before end-to-end closeout.

EMW-1.1 User-Directed Result — 12 August 2026

The active configuration is now docs_scopes_v4, with external private media rooted at $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/docs-viewer/media. The user owns the file move/copy; Docs Viewer owns recognition and future operations at the new locations. Acceptance is counts-only: no migration manifest, persistent hash catalogue, or automated byte mover was created.

The external workspace currently resolves 447 ready media objects, one registered Mermaid build source, and one source-evidence file:

All five real scope document and search builds completed without warnings. The local Analysis HTML route resolves coincidence-salience-demo.html from the external workspace with the sandboxed HTML response contract. Canonical media tokens are unchanged. Existing Analysis repository public media and R2 configuration remain untouched; public-media copying and stale cleanup are explicitly deferred to EMW-1.2.

Former private locations contain no media objects. Marker-only legacy directories do not participate in docs_scopes_v4 and carry no authority. Stop here for review; do not begin EMW-1.2 without explicit approval.

Marker files and .DS_Store are not media identities. All 447 ready objects migrate whether currently referenced or not. The notable unreferenced set is three Studio objects, three Analysis objects, four Notes objects, 23 Processing download packages, and dotlineform/img/d-20260801-212422-dc8979-image-01.webp. Unreferenced state does not confer deletion authority.

Analysis currently exposes all 38 ready objects publicly because its active ready locations are already site/ or R2. The current public payload snapshot references only img/beyond-conscious-subconscious-image-01.png and html/coincidence-salience-demo.html; its public-reference fingerprint is 14fefbc725045e3e6dc76b62f7068a6366baacb22cc1201a0e6dbb20927b1428. EMW-1.1 must preserve all 38 public objects. EMW-1.2 must derive a fresh prospective publishable reference set and preview any stale removal rather than treating this snapshot as deletion permission.

The configured Analysis R2 prefix contains two PDF identities totalling 860,228 bytes plus an exact prefix-marker object. Both PDFs were retrieved successfully, their listed and downloaded sizes match, and both currently have SHA-256 d53a2b1344ac8d9b2b2f7821f37dc50a3b6f7bba91de450a545f350a5f6a67a6; the distinct logical identities must remain distinct. The current R2 adapter's list path raises on the zero-length prefix marker, so EMW inventory and reconciliation must explicitly ignore exact directory-marker keys.

R2 also contains marker-only library and studio namespaces and 111 non-marker moments/img objects totalling 19,317,698 bytes. Those scopes are not in the current configured parent-scope set, so EMW-1 neither migrates nor deletes those objects. Resolving their ownership would be a separate cleanup decision.

The proposed $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/docs-viewer/media/ root does not yet exist. No current logical {scope, media type, identity} appears on more than one active filesystem or R2 surface. Five .DS_Store files and the current tracked or remote marker objects are excluded from the migration manifest and removed only when an exact obsolete private directory is cleaned after cutover.

Frozen External Folder Contract

$DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/
  docs-viewer/
    media/
      studio/
        files/
        img/
        svg/
        build-source/
          mermaid/
      analysis/
        files/

        img/

        build-source/

          mermaid/

  • This is the exact configured directory set to create. One configured parent scope owns one exact namespace. Sub-scopes reuse it and never create a media subdirectory.
  • Empty external directories need no .gitkeep. Analysis media-source-evidence.json is a file copied to media/analysis/media-source-evidence.json during migration, not another directory; the file may be absent in other scopes until a row exists.
  • Ready-media and build-source identities remain one safe flat filename. Nested identities, filename inference, cross-scope physical sharing, and content-derived names are not introduced.
  • The configured workspace root, scope directory, type directory, and identity must remain real non-symlink paths beneath the exact workspace root. Server operations reject traversal, symlink escape, wrong scope/type, and browser-supplied absolute paths.
  • Retained originals remain beneath configured Projects-relative source roots such as analysis/ or processing/. They are not copied into this folder except through an explicit Add/Import derivation to a managed identity.
  • media-source-evidence.json keeps schema docs_media_source_evidence_v1 and its exact {media_type, identity, source_root, source_path} rows; only its owner path changes.
  • The external workspace is the sole private authority after cutover, not a backup system. Existing user-managed backup or synchronization policy must cover it; EMW adds no backup service, replica, recovery catalogue, or health promise.
  • Configuration parsing and document-only URL rendering normalize this marker without requiring the workspace to exist. Add, Import media materialization, inventory, serving, Copy, build-source work, lifecycle mutation, and media projection resolve availability at their own server-side boundary and report unavailable without reading old private or public bytes as fallback.

Frozen Configuration Split

docs_scopes_v4 should express one global external workspace, one provider-free managed contract per scope, and optional public media projections. Unchanged document, search, route, and sub-scope fields are omitted from this schematic.

{
  "schema_version": "docs_scopes_v4",
  "media_workspace": {
    "location": {
      "provider": "external_local",
      "path": "$DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/docs-viewer/media"
    }
  },
  "scopes": [
    {
      "scope_id": "analysis",
      "source": {},
      "media": {
        "types": {
          "img": {"build_inputs": []},
          "svg": {"build_inputs": ["mermaid"]},
          "files": {"build_inputs": []},
          "html": {"build_inputs": []}
        },
        "build_sources": {
          "mermaid": {"producer": "mermaid", "publishes_to": "svg"}
        }
      },
      "public_projection": {
        "documents": {"location": {"provider": "repository", "path": "site/assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis"}},
        "search": {"location": {"provider": "repository", "path": "site/assets/data/search/analysis/index.json"}},
        "media": {
          "img": {"location": {"provider": "repository", "path": "site/assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/media/img"}, "served_path_prefix": "/assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/media/img"}
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

The scope ID and registered type derive the managed location <workspace>/<scope>/<type>, logical reference docs/<scope>/<type>, and Manage prefix /docs/media/<scope>/<type>. A registered build-source type derives <workspace>/<scope>/build-source/<type>. Evidence derives <workspace>/<scope>/media-source-evidence.json. These paths and prefixes are invariants, not repeated provider choices.

For a public scope, public_projection.media must contain the same type keys as media.types; each record owns one repository target beneath the exact tracked site/.../<scope>/media/<type> path or one R2 target at docs/<scope>/<type>, plus its public served prefix. A local scope keeps public_projection: null. The loader rejects the v3 published.media, source.build_media, managed location, and combined managed/public served-prefix fields after the cutover; there is no alias, old-schema reader, fallback, or dual write.

The current public target policy is frozen:

scope/type public target public served prefix
Analysis img repository site/assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/media/img /assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/media/img
Analysis svg repository site/assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/media/svg /assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/media/svg
Analysis html repository site/assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/media/html /assets/data/docs/scopes/analysis/media/html
Analysis files R2 docs/analysis/files https://media.dotlineform.com/docs/analysis/files

Scope Create retains its current public-scope default split—R2 for img and files, repository for svg, and no default html type—while creating every new scope's private managed namespace externally. EMW-1 does not consolidate those public targets.

Manage And Public Rendering Seam

  • Main-scope and sub-scope working payloads render every same-scope logical token to the derived Manage prefix. The builder does not require the managed byte to exist and does not use a public target as a read fallback.
  • The generated Manage browser config publishes Manage prefixes. The generated public browser config publishes the corresponding public_projection.media prefixes; no physical path is browser-visible.
  • Publish already computes the exact prospective parent and sub-scope payload files after publishability and report/Mermaid projection. EMW-1.2 should reuse that set, inspect real HTML src and href attributes under exact Manage prefixes, union {type, identity}, and rewrite those attributes to the configured public prefixes. Fenced examples, code text, comments, foreign-scope URLs, and arbitrary prose are not references.
  • The current docs_media_inventory.py source regex is not sufficient for Publish: it scans only parent source in its top-level helper, counts literal/commented examples, and the R2 adapter currently rejects a prefix marker. The existing inventory boundary should be corrected to consume exact parent/sub-scope payloads and marker-safe adapters rather than adding a second registry.
  • html-media keeps the existing sandboxed iframe. Manage adds exact /docs/media/<scope>/html/<filename>.html serving from the external workspace with text/html, no-store, nosniff, and a response CSP matching the existing review-asset sandbox boundary; ordinary file downloads remain attachments. Public HTML continues to use the frozen public target and iframe sandbox.
  • Publish projects public URLs even when the managed object is missing. It copies and byte-verifies each available referenced object independently, retains an existing public object while its identity remains referenced, and deletes only public identities absent from the complete prospective reference set. Media absence or copy failure is reported but does not roll back or block document/search publication.
  • Document Delete and unpublish do not delete managed bytes. Scope-wide Publish owns shared public-media reconciliation; explicit whole-scope lifecycle remains the only scope-level deletion boundary.

Superseded Migration Plan

This was the pre-approval migration proposal. It was not executed. The user explicitly selected a direct manual move/copy with counts-only acceptance and no migration manifest or hashes. The steps below are preserved solely to explain the earlier review assumptions.

  1. Stop Docs Viewer media writers and the watcher, regenerate the exact manifest, compare this checkpoint's counts and fingerprints, and stop for review on any drift that changes the accepted shape.
  2. Preflight the configured Projects base, real non-symlink workspace/scope/type paths, available space, user-owned backup expectation, empty-or-byte-identical targets, and read capability for every repository, external-local, and R2 source.
  3. Copy every manifest row to its final external identity while v3 remains the sole active authority. Retrieve both configured R2 objects; never infer them from site/, another identity, or matching bytes.
  4. Re-read every external target and verify size plus SHA-256. Any missing, different, unreadable, or unlisted source blocks cutover. No partial target becomes active.
  5. With v4 code and focused tests prepared and the service still stopped, atomically replace the one scope config, restart once, and verify Add/Import destinations, inventory, evidence, registered build sources, Manage serving, Copy, static snapshot/export, and lifecycle paths through the new namespace. No process runs a mixed schema.
  6. Preserve all existing Analysis site/ and R2 objects. They are public projections after cutover and remain untouched until an EMW-1.2 Publish preview and confirmation.
  7. After every active owner verifies against v4, remove only manifest-owned obsolete private roots: repository Studio/Processing published/media, repository build-source/evidence remnants, and external-local Notes/Dotlineform source/media or published/media. Remove their exact markers, .DS_Store, and empty directories; do not touch retained originals, current public site//R2 bytes, or unconfigured R2 namespaces.

Before configuration cutover, rollback means discarding only exact manifest-created targets while the unchanged v3 authority remains live. After cutover but before old-root cleanup, rollback restores the single config/code set and restarts against the untouched old roots. After cleanup, recovery may rehydrate an old root from the verified external rows and manifest, but runtime never gains a dual reader or generic transaction framework.

EMW-1.1 is expected to change roughly 850–1,250 production lines and 1,000–1,600 focused test lines across these existing seams, plus the v4 config, migration evidence, external copies, and exact obsolete-private-path removals. EMW-1.2 is expected to change roughly 450–750 production lines and 700–1,100 focused test lines around prospective reference extraction, URL projection, repository/R2 copy and stale cleanup, shared retention, missing-media independence, and Publish reporting. These are review estimates, not a frozen file plan.

Focused EMW-1.1 evidence should cover v4 validation and retired-field rejection; lazy unavailable-workspace behavior; path and symlink confinement; Add/Import/evidence/inventory; Mermaid intake/build/watch; local image/file/SVG/HTML serving; exact Copy; static media snapshot; scope create/rename/delete; a disposable mixed-provider migration rehearsal; the real identity/count/hash reconciliation; changed Python/JavaScript lint; and git diff --check. EMW-1.2 should add pure prospective reference extraction, parent/sub-scope publishability, comments/examples, shared identities, missing managed objects, independent copy failure, repository and R2 verification, exact stale deletion, browser-config and payload URL projection, HTML, site validation, and focused route/module evidence.

Risks And Stop Conditions

  • The first media-aware Analysis Publish may have a large stale-public diff because 38 public media objects exist while the current public payload snapshot references two. EMW-1.1 preserves all 38; EMW-1.2 requires an explicit fresh preview.
  • Scope Create, Rename, and Delete currently treat scope-local media as part of the document scope root. Leaving those owners on v3 would create orphaned or wrongly deleted external namespaces, so lifecycle is part of the cutover rather than optional cleanup.
  • Eager external path resolution would make repository-backed document builds depend on workspace availability. V4 must keep configuration and URL projection read-only/lazy and fail only at the media operation boundary.
  • HTML local serving is a security boundary. If it cannot reuse the current sandbox/CSP model without changing public HTML trust, stop and review that separately.
  • A public copy must never become private authority merely because an external target is missing. A copy failure reports degraded media while document publication continues.
  • Stop before implementation if the result needs a general asset registry, nested identity migration, content-addressing, deduplication, provider fallback, background synchronization, backup installation, arbitrary R2 cleanup, dual authority, or a generic transaction/recovery framework.

EMW-1 Evidence And Next Gate

  • Live read-only inventory completed across repository, external-local, site/, and R2 surfaces for all five configured parent scopes.
  • Every managed/build/evidence byte was read and hashed; both configured R2 objects were retrieved and size-verified.
  • Working parent and sub-scope payload references were reconciled against active ready identities with zero missing rendered identities.
  • Current public target policy, proposed external root absence, unreferenced objects, marker behavior, legacy unconfigured R2 namespaces, and current inventory-helper limitations are recorded above.
  • EMW-1.0 changed no runtime source, active configuration, managed byte, public byte, or obsolete path.
  • EMW-1.1 activated the external contract and recognized the user-relocated files without adding a manifest, hashes, compatibility reader, or public-copy fallback.
  • Exact external counts reconcile to 447 ready objects, one registered build source, and one evidence file; all five real document and search builds completed without warnings.
  • Existing Analysis public repository media and R2 targets remain untouched.

The relocation evidence in this record is complete. Current implementation and review status belong to EMW-1; this temporary record grants no authority to apply the live Analysis Publish preview or begin closeout.
